title: Victoria Falls (Mosi-oa-Tunya)
summary: Victoria Falls, called Mosi-oa-Tunya, lies on the Zambezi on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe. UNESCO gives the curtain of falling water as 1708 m wide with a deepest point of 108 m. David Livingstone set out to visit it in 1855, according to the Zambia Tourism Agency.

uncertainty.note: Year of Livingstone's visit as given by the Zambia Tourism page; the falls are far older and no age for them was found on an opened page.

as_recorded.value: it was only in 1855 that he set out to visit it

where.modern_name: Victoria Falls / Mosi-oa-Tunya, Zambia and Zimbabwe
where.historical_name: Mosi-oa-Tunya, the smoke that thunders, on the Zambezi; named Victoria Falls by Livingstone

importance.justification: World Heritage waterfall, described by UNESCO as the largest curtain of falling water in the world.

reviewer_note: The date is Livingstone's 1855 visit, not the age of the falls; no opened page gave a geological age. UNESCO coordinates S17 55 28.308 E25 51 19.404 converted to decimals; Wikidata -17.9248, 25.8581. No model (natural feature).
